idiom_name: record with init-only properties + with-expressions (+ System.Collections.Immutable)
implementation_notes: C# ships the value half of immutability as syntax: a positional record declares init-only properties, a readonly record struct adds value equality for structs, and with-expressions are the built-in wither, so an update is written next = current with { Port = p }. For collections the BCL provides System.Collections.Immutable (ImmutableArray<T>, ImmutableList<T>, ImmutableDictionary<K,V>) whose Add, SetItem and Remove return new instances that share structure, replacing hand-written copy-copy-freeze code, while System.Collections.Frozen covers read-optimized lookup tables that are built once and never change. The classic defensive-copy form is still justified where a framework contract demands mutation (serializers, EF entities): map to records at the edge. Where a large graph is built incrementally, use the ImmutableArray<T>.Builder / ImmutableDictionary<K,V>.Builder instead of a with-expression per change and freeze once with ToImmutable.
pitfalls: with-expressions copy shallowly: mutable reference members (arrays, List<T>, plain dictionaries) stay shared, so mutating them changes every supposedly immutable copy.
default(ImmutableArray<T>) is uninitialized and throws when accessed; initialize fields with ImmutableArray.Create/Empty and test IsDefault.
readonly on a field or init-only on a property freezes the reference, not the object it points to, so a readonly member of a mutable type can still be mutated.
